rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 "H1/lede": line 9: "the compound step closes Kieran Klaassen's loop: ideate → brainstorm → plan → work → review → polish → compound → repeat" — this is the ONLY place this file itself defines 'the loop,' and it prints a full 8-stage sequence ending in 'repeat.' chunk 4 "Close the session": line 55: "The loop's last move, closing the bug's ticket outside the repo, is the homework" — uses bare 'the loop' to mean a different sequence (the module's own orient→fix→compound→close arc, whose last step is close-the-ticket, per getting-going.md line 40: "The loop is orient → fix → compound → close"). That second sequence is never named anywhere in THIS file; it only resolves via the enclosing module's signposting. Under the sequential-deck-read rule, chunk 0's freshly printed, textually prominent, attributed ("Kieran Klaassen's") 8-stage sequence is the reader's most recent and most detailed definition of 'the loop' by the time they reach chunk 4 — and by its own terms the loop's last move is 'repeat,' not 'close the ticket.' The disambiguating 'Klaassen's' qualifier is present only on first mention and dropped at chunk 4, so a cold sequential reader has no in-file signal that 'the loop' has silently switched referents. Before this pass printed the full sequence, chunk 0 gave no rival stage-list, so bare 'the loop' cleanly defaulted to the module's arc throughout the file; printing the sequence is what created the two-candidate ambiguity. (A prior instance of this verdict, run before today's edit, waved this through as resolving to chunk 0 without checking that chunk 0's actual last-named stage doesn't match chunk 4's claim — that's the gap this re-run catches.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either keep the printed Klaassen sequence but stop calling it 'the loop' unqualified later in the file (say 'this module's four-move loop' at chunk 4), or drop the colon-and-stage-list at chunk 0 back to a bare attribution so this file only ever carries one definition of 'the loop.'
Chunk 4 line 55 names the claim itself ("closing the bug's ticket outside the repo") rather than pointing at close-the-ticket.md by position. No positional cross-file pointer found in the body.
